title: Week 19 Check-In · How I Became a Ghost
description: This week Isaac's family joined the Choctaw walkers on the road west. You practiced strong verbs and active voice, the roots anim and spir, and the endings -ive, -al and -ic. Show what you know.

questions.label: Identification
questions.text: Which sentence is in the active voice?
options: The houses were burned in the night.
The older women sang the Choctaw death song.
The blankets were handed out from the wagons.
Shoes were cut from a blanket.
questions.status: kept (a fourth option added; the right sentence is from Ch. 11)

questions.label: Rewrite
questions.text: Rewrite this sentence in the active voice. Make sure the reader knows who did the action.
questions.excerpt: Blanket shoes were tied on Nita’s feet.
questions.key: Isaac tied blanket shoes on Nita’s feet. (Any active sentence with Isaac as the subject.)
questions.from: 19.2 Grammar (rewrite in the active voice); Ch. 9
questions.status: changed (the old sentence was about Ch. 6 blankets; this one is from this week's chapters)

questions.label: Explain
questions.text: A history writer could say “Isaac’s town was burned” or “The Nahullos burned Isaac’s town.” Which version is better for writing about history? Explain what the other version hides.
questions.key: The active version. The passive version hides who did it; it never names the Nahullos.
questions.from: 19.4 Grammar (active voice names who is responsible)
questions.status: fixed (the old item said soldiers burned the town; in the book it was the Nahullos)

questions.label: Root Identification
questions.text: The root anim means “life, spirit.” The root spir means “breathe.” Which word has the root that means “breathe”?

questions.label: Context Clues
questions.text: Read the sentences from Chapter 10. What does vanished most likely mean?
questions.excerpt: “Then another voice cut through the snow. ‘Son!’ It was my father’s voice. The Choctaw ghosts vanished.”

questions.label: Use It
questions.text: Use the word refused in a sentence that shows you know what it means. Connect it to something Isaac does in Chapter 10 or 11.
questions.key: Uses refused correctly (said no firmly). Ch. 10: Isaac refused to look behind him. Ch. 11: he had learned never to refuse a gift.

questions.label: Add the Ending
questions.text: Add -ive, -al or -ic to make a describing word. Write all three: protect → ___   season → ___   hero → ___

questions.label: Spot It
questions.text: Which describing word is spelled correctly?

questions.label: Tricky Bases
questions.text: Add -ive to create and -al to nature. Write both new words. What happened to the base word each time?
questions.key: creative, natural. The final e drops before the vowel ending.

questions.label: Detail
questions.text: What does Isaac do after his father says these words? What happens to his feet afterward?
questions.key: He stops looking behind him, keeps walking and forgets the pain. Three days later his feet heal (the healing began with his father’s words).

questions.label: Inference
questions.text: In Chapter 9, Isaac promises to be Nita’s big brother and take care of her. How do Isaac and Nita take care of each other in Chapters 9 to 11? What does Nita’s death in Chapter 11 mean for Isaac’s promise? Use at least two details from two different chapters.
questions.key: 2 pts: two details from two chapters. Ch. 9: he cuts blanket shoes for her feet. Ch. 11: she gives him her shoes; he cuts her another pair. Her death means he can no longer keep the promise while she is alive (Mister Jonah taught him the dead can still help the living). 1 pt: one detail or one chapter.

questions.label: Read Like a Writer
questions.text: Write two sentences with I about a time you were very cold, tired or hungry. First give one detail only you could feel. Then give one plain reaction.
questions.excerpt: “My feet were freezing cold and burning hot at the same time. I never knew pain could hurt this bad.”
questions.key: Two first-person sentences: a felt detail, then a plain reaction (thoughts, details, reactions).
questions.from: 19.3 Read Like a Writer (first-person voice: a detail, then a reaction)
questions.status: changed (the old model taught a pattern this week's Read Like a Writer no longer teaches)

questions.label: Short Response
questions.text: In Chapter 8, Isaac says, “The smallpox blankets were ghost-making blankets.” In 2–3 sentences, explain why Isaac’s family waits before taking blankets on the walk, and how Mister Jonah’s ghost helps them decide.
questions.key: They remember the swamp blankets carried smallpox. Mister Jonah’s ghost tells Isaac the new blankets are safe, so his father asks for blankets in the morning.

passage.title: Reading passage (Chapter 10)
passage.text:
“Son,” he said, “you cannot keep your eyes on the bloody footprints you have left behind you. You must keep your eyes on where you are going.”
I took a deep breath. I nodded. From that moment on, even though my feet burned, I refused to look behind me. I looked where I was going and forgot about the pain.
passage.cite: Tim Tingle, How I Became a Ghost, Chapter 10
